To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) we report the second case of an ABCA1 splice mutation causing low HDL-C levels and 2) we describe the first case of two ABCA1 splice mutations in a family with low HDL- C and premature CHD

1) two novel splice variants in the ABCA1 gene have been identified in a family with low levels of high density lipoprotein (HDL-C) and premature coronary heart disease, and 2) the mutations cause skipping of Exons 7 and 32, resulting respectively in the elimination of the 59 amino acids of the first extracellular ABCA1 loop and 8 novel amino acid residues, followed by a stop-codon and a predicted protein of 1496 amino acids
two novel ABCA1 splice variants were identified in a patient with low HDL cholesterol and premature coronary heart disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genetic mutations that cause low levels of high density lipoprotein (HDL-C) and premature coronary disease, and the characterization of the resulting protein defects.
the identification and characterization of mutations in ABCA 1 that are associated with low HDL and premature coronary disease.
the molecular mechanisms of the genetic etiology of hypoalphalipoproteinemias.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the first report of 2 different splice defects in the ABCA1 gene causing a low HDL-C phenotype and CHD in an affected individual and his family members.
these mutations are likely to be pathologic and contribute to the low HDL-C and CHD risk of this proband and family.
this is a novel mutation in the ABCA1 gene that results in a severe form of HDL deficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the identification of splice variants is important for the accurate determination of the molecular basis of disease.
the ABCA1 gene is a complex gene with multiple splice junctions, and the identification of multiple mutations in the same gene in a single patient is a rare finding.
2 novel mutations in ABCA11 were found to cause low HDL in a family with premature coronary disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the identification of splice mutations can be challenging and requires careful analysis of cDNA.
the identification of splice defects is important to the understanding and treatment of patients with premature CHD.
splice defects in ABC1 should be considered when screening for ABCA1 mutations.
